answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is never free. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations, each cost blowing in like a gale off the wharf. The toll climbs with head count, so cheap mass registration stalls against compute no zephyr-light shortcut can fake away.
